summary: Iteration 15 verifies the two new 'G-code per Utensile' + 'Fuga vs Bordo' features. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases pass — GET /api/tools returns 5 tools including BORDO (cyan #06B6D4, ACI 4, T5); per-tool G-code export (project + boat-nested) emits '===== <TOOL>' sections with proper M6 T<n> / M3 S<rpm> / M5-between-tool-changes and per-tool feed & depth; DXF exports (project + boat nested-dxf + boat export/dxf) include BORDO layer with cyan color; Element.tool='BORDO' routes to BORDO layer. Frontend: RIEMPI modal correctly renders both 'Utensile fughe interne' (FUGA/CONTORNO/TAGLIO) and, when style=BORDATO or SOLO BORDO, 'Utensile bordatura' chips (BORDO/CONTORNO/FUGA) with the italian hint 'La bordatura teak usa un utensile diverso dalle fughe interne.' Tapping RIEMPI confirm with BORDATO + groove=0 correctly creates TWO fill elements sharing a group id (tool=BORDO role=border + tool=FUGA role=pattern) and the resulting DXF uses both BORDO and FUGA layers. Editor TEXTURE tab no longer crashes (previous iteration's toolColor prop bug is fixed). CRITICAL BACKEND BUG FOUND: geometry/fill for style=bordato with groove_mm>0 (the common CNC case) collapses the border into `pattern` and returns border_count=0 — so the frontend split silently degrades to a single FUGA element and the BORDO layer never gets any polylines. Only groove_mm=0 produces the intended two-tool split.

critical.issue: geometry_ops.fill_pattern collapses `border_lines` into caulking pockets and returns border=[] whenever groove_mm>0 (see /app/backend/geometry_ops.py lines 576-591). Result: the new 'Fuga vs Bordo' feature only splits into two tool elements when groove_mm=0. Any real teak preset (default groove 4–5mm) makes the RIEMPI/BORDATO flow produce a single FUGA fill and NO BORDO polylines in the DXF/G-code — defeating the whole feature. Fix suggestion: keep the raw `border_lines` in the returned `border` field even when caulking pockets consume them (either return them alongside `pattern`, or expose a separate `border_grooved` list). Frontend runFill splits on r.border, so backend must always return border for bordato/bordo.

integration_issues.flow: RIEMPI · BORDATO with caulking groove (default groove_mm ≥ 1)
integration_issues.issue: Because backend returns border_count=0, hasBorder is false in runFill and the code falls back to a single-element fill (tool=FUGA). The 'Utensile bordatura' chip is honored ONLY when groove_mm=0. This is an end-user-visible gap: selecting BORDO for 'Utensile bordatura' has no effect for any teak-style preset (which sets groove=5 for 'doghe').

Verify with curl `/api/geometry/fill … pattern=lines style=bordato groove_mm=5 …` returning border_count>0, then re-tap RIEMPI in the editor and confirm two fill elements (BORDO+FUGA) persist in GET /api/projects/{id}.

rca_of_issue: Bug: RIEMPI/BORDATO does not actually route the teak border to the BORDO tool for any real teak preset. RCA: /app/backend/geometry_ops.py fill_pattern (lines ~509-591) builds `border_lines` for style in ('bordato','bordo'). When groove_mm>0 it turns border_lines into thin caulking pockets by appending them into a pockets list and then either (a) returns pattern=<pockets rings> with border=[] (line 589), or (b) returns pattern=[] with border=<pockets rings> only when the interior clip is empty (line 588). In case (a) — the common case for teak doghe/bordato — the frontend receives border_count=0, so runFill's hasBorder check fails and it falls back to a single fill element on the pattern tool (FUGA). Reproduction: POST /api/geometry/fill with pattern=lines style=bordato groove_mm=5 border_mm=40 → response.border_count=0 despite border being visually rendered. Mitigation: keep `border` field populated with the border geometry (either the raw ring polylines or the border-derived caulking pockets) whenever style ∈ {bordato,bordo}; the frontend split relies solely on r.border being non-empty.
